posts.text: Meta releases its first frontier model, Muse Wonder. Where Muse Spark aimed to be a lightweight model that could perform at low latency, the Wonder models are larger and said to be more capable, with higher benchmark scores and better results on complex tasks like coding.

posts.author: Bloomberg Tech
posts.text: Barclays: “Generational Shift” in Aerospace & Defense. Anthony Valentini of Barclays says aerospace and defense is at an inflection point: newer, high-growth companies using commercial business models should be evaluated differently from traditional contractors and could achieve higher margins at scale. He describes the shift toward lower-cost autonomous systems as a generational change, with new entrants positioned to gain market share over the next decade. He speaks with Scarlet Fu & Hema Parmar on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

posts.text: Neostellar’s Willy Lee on AI Landscape Ahead of Anthropic Pre-IPO Investor Day. Willy Lee, Principal at Neostellar, says attention on Anthropic’s potential IPO risks obscuring broader AI investment and adoption. He cited nearly $200 billion in U.S. venture capital deployed in the first half of the year—more than 74% of the prior year’s estimated total. He speaks with Scarlet Fu & Hema Parmar on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

posts.author: Bloomberg Tech
posts.text: Cisco, Nvidia Tackle AI’s Growing Data Center Bottleneck. Cisco is partnering with Nvidia on a new generation of optical networking technology designed to handle the exploding amount of data moving through AI data centers. Cisco President and Chief Product Officer Jeetu Patel explains why increasingly powerful AI agents could consume far more network bandwidth than humans performing the same tasks, and how faster, more power-efficient connections could help hundreds of thousands of GPUs operate together while lowering the cost of AI. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

posts.author: The Decoder
posts.text: Microsoft plans to scale its own Maia AI chips to gigawatt levels by 2027. Microsoft will make its in-house Azure Maia chips the main AI inference system across its products starting in 2027, deploying them at multi-gigawatt scale. The upcoming Maia 300 should deliver 40 percent more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems. CEO Satya Nadella calls it "our biggest bet yet on our own silicon."
